title: Customer-facing Erasure Transcript Service
creator: Ellen Martinez
description: Deliver a customer-facing, tamper-evident transcript of data erasure activity for Right‑to‑Be‑Forgotten (RTBF) requests. The transcript is an auditable chronological record (human- and machine-readable) that customers can download from the Console or fetch via API. It will summarize deletion actions, scope (tenant/region), timestamps, responsible service/worker IDs, and a cryptographic signature anchored to our KMS to provide non-repudiation. This solves customer requests for verifiable proof of deletion without exposing internal logs or PII.
acceptance_criteria: Transcript export API (/v1/erasure-transcripts/{tenant_id}/{request_id}) returns a signed JSONL bundle containing all expunge events for the RTBF request and a signed manifest with checksum within 30s of expunge completion.
Console: per-request page shows a 'Download Erasure Transcript' button that produces the same signed bundle and displays high-level summary (items deleted count, regional stamp, signed_at timestamp).
Transcript bundles are stored in tenant-scoped, region-stamped S3 buckets with retention and access controls matching existing evidence storage policies.

Each bundle contains an ordered list of events (created_at, object_type, object_id redaction token, worker_id, expunge_step, outcome) and a manifest with SHA-256 checksum and signature from KMS; signature verifies against a published public key.
Automated test harness verifies end-to-end generation: trigger RTBF via sandbox tenant -> run expunge -> transcript available and signature verifies -> contents redact PII as per schema.
Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained for transcript fields and retention period documented in Confluence.

Performance: transcript generation adds <= 5s latency to the final expunge completion path for typical request sizes (<= 10k objects). For large requests, generation is async and Console shows 'processing' state with estimated completion time.
scope_included: Generate signed, ordered transcript bundles for RTBF and tenant-initiated bulk erasures
Expose transcript via Console UI and REST API
Region-aware storage and per-tenant access controls
Signed manifest with checksum and KMS-backed signature
Automated e2e tests and Confluence runbook for auditors
scope_excluded: Reprocessing historical requests older than retention window (handled by separate expunge backfill project)
Deep forensics of cross-tenant multi-region replication beyond providing event chronology
technical_notes: Orchestrator: extend expunge-orchestrator to emit canonical event records to evidence-writer after each stage (mark, copy, delete, tombstone). Events are immutable and append-only.

Bundle generation: evidence-writer composes JSONL ordered by event sequence, computes SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 bytes, requests KMS to sign digest, attaches signature in manifest.json and uploads bundle to region/tenant path.
Storage: tenant/region S3 with server-side encryption; ACLs copied from existing evidence buckets. Use lifecycle policies consistent with compliance retention (configurable per-tenant).

API: new endpoint /v1/erasure-transcripts/{tenant_id}/{request_id} that validates caller identity and returns pre-signed S3 link for bundle, or streams JSONL when requested by authorized service accounts.
Console: add Transcript tab to RTBF request detail page; display summary metrics and 'Download' action that calls API and surfaces verifyable signature information.
Scaling: avoid blocking expunge critical path for very large deletes — allow async bundle finalization job; Console will poll status. Small deletes (<10k events) generate inline within expunge job.
Security: use KMS HSM-backed signing key with rotation policy; publish verification public key to our compliance endpoint for customer verification.
Redaction: transcript contains redaction tokens (deterministic per-tenant salt) instead of raw PII. Tokenization algorithm and salt management to be approved by Security and Privacy.
Auditing: every transcript generation emits a telemetry event for observability and billing (if we offer paid attestations later).
